audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave (W) is described four times as a heal that 'heals your poke back' and as 'sustain'. It is a shield. Fate Sealed (R) is also called a knockup twice — it is a pull.
audit.why: Riot's text: W 'Cleaves forward, damaging all enemies in a cone. Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit', 700 range, 14s, cooldown scaling with attack speed. R 'blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him', 1000 range, 120/100/80s. Only Mortal Steel's third cast is a knockup.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave = a shield that must be forced out before committing burst; Fate Sealed = a pull; the knockup is Mortal Steel's third cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four level rows disagree with the packet chart and the matchup's own why text: Level 1 is Kennen although whys[0] says it reads even, Level 2 is 'Skill' and Level 3 is Yone although whys[1] and whys[2] describe Kennen's cleanest early window, and First item is Yone although whys[5] calls it Kennen's peak relative strength.
audit.why: Mortal Steel is 450 range against a 950-range Q, and Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, so the chip windows between his cooldowns belong to Kennen through first item. Levels 4-5 and 2+ items are correctly his.
audit.corrected: Level 1 = Skill, Level 2 = Kennen, Level 3 = Kennen, First item = Kennen.

audit.why: Kennen at 2-3, level 6 and first item is right, and Yone's takeover at two items is right. Worth noting Fate Sealed at rank 3 is 80s against Kennen's flat 120s R, so late he has his ultimate roughly every other fight Kennen does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late paragraph tells the reader the matchup 'reads TRICKY' while diff is EVEN and the final rating line says Even matchup.
audit.why: Two different difficulty labels render on the same page.
audit.corrected: Late paragraph now says it reads even.

edits.before: Yone's lane is even at level 1 but you get the first real window — you out-range his Q (Mortal Steel) with Thundering Shuriken, so chip him at max range and start stacking Mark of the Storm while he just farms. At 2-3 your second Q point plus Electrical Surge on-hit lets you land a genuine poke trade or even a two-mark stun if he oversteps to last-hit. The catch: his Q stacks and W-cleave heal a lot of your poke back, so chunk-and-back rather than expecting it to stick. Never get marked into his Q3 knockup-dash with no E to escape.
edits.after: Yone's lane is even at level 1 but you get the first real window — Thundering Shuriken reaches 950 against his 450-range Mortal Steel, so chip him at max range and stack Mark of the Storm while he farms. At 2-3 your second Q point plus Electrical Surge on-hit lets you land a genuine poke trade or even a two-mark stun if he oversteps to last-hit. The catch: Spirit Cleave shields off a chunk of your poke every 14 seconds, so chunk-and-back rather than expecting it to stick. Never get caught by his third Mortal Steel knockup-dash with no E to escape.

edits.before: This is where Yone reclaims the lane and why it reads TRICKY — at 2+ items his sustain, Q-dash mobility and R knockup let him survive your stun window and out-duel you once your R is on cooldown, and you're a squishy caster he can pin and burst. You must close on your 6 and first-item spike; if the game goes long, stop trying to solo-duel him in the sidelane and pivot to a teamfight engager where your AoE R and global threat catch his whole team instead of his one slippery body.
edits.after: This is where Yone reclaims the lane and why it only reads even — at 2+ items his Spirit Cleave shield, Mortal Steel mobility and Fate Sealed pull let him survive your stun window and out-duel you once your R is down, and Fate Sealed is 80s to your 120s. notes: Corrected a repeated mechanic error: Spirit Cleave was written as a heal in four places and Fate Sealed as a knockup in two. Riot's text gives W a shield scaling with champions hit, and R a pull; the only knockup is Mortal Steel's third cast. Level chart rows 0, 1, 2 and 5 flipped as one atomic group across both layers. Whether Soul Unbound's spirit form dodges an already-applied Mark of the Storm is not in the kit data and was not asserted.
